limits: Timings are individual observations under concurrent verification, not a stable performance trend. Static scale covers two selected targets and 4/8/16/32/64 swap registrations; it does not establish arbitrary graph complexity.

All 45 preexisting native cases retain identical resource counters. Callable-flow IR/bitcode grow by 16/4 bytes, and owner-factories IR/bitcode shrink by 12/4 bytes. A separately regenerated callable fixture differs only in a generated context type suffix; no broader semantic-equivalence claim is inferred from byte counts.

The composed fixture covers direct/native/recursive setters, distinct selected targets, prepared borrowed operands, scalar/callable/regional pointers, branches, repeated swaps, checked null failure, recovery, return replacement, selected borrowed returns and regional-slot closure capture.

Native injection verifies unpublished registration cannot rebind its target, prior actions drain, and 10000 dynamic swaps retain all records until the enclosing full scope exits. All records/images/regions release exactly once.

An initially ownerless null pointer first rebound during cleanup still hits the explicit unfinished-flow guard. An immediate read at a repeated loop entry can still lose a non-null invariant before its per-iteration deferred rebind. Per-iteration cleanup with an unconditional setter and a post-loop read is accepted by the recorded probe. These are implementation observations, not new language rules.

Ownership mutation/owning deferred operands, conditional owner/queue correlation, remaining target/loop/result correlations, generic capture transport and process-lifetime module queues remain incomplete. AOT family integration, actual-owner/abstract-result evidence and D-22 construction mechanisms retain their existing boundaries. No runtime bookkeeping, regional layout, allocator protocol, numeric/fraction behavior or new source policy is introduced.
